bug_semantics: FileBinding.write and ZipFileBinding.write join a FileCredentials-supplied name onto a per-build secrets directory with FilePath.child and then copyFrom/unzipFrom that path. FilePath.child honors ../ and path separators, so a credential whose getFileName() is a traversal payload (e.g. ../../../../p0wn3d.txt, as in Security3672Test) writes the secret bytes (or extracts a zip) outside the intended UUID secrets dir on the node filesystem. If a low-privileged user can supply file/zip credentials used by a job on the built-in node, the write can land under JENKINS_HOME (init.groovy.d, plugins) and become RCE. FileCredentials javadoc claimed a simple basename, but the binding never enforced that contract; FileCredentialsImpl UI upload strips prefixes, yet programmatic/XML constructors and other implementations can return unsanitized names.
flaw_origin: The unsanitized child(credentials.getFileName()) write was first authored in jenkinsci/plain-credentials-plugin FileBinding.bind in root commit 83f3ca6dbf7f8311d355cd49559447d53090e034 (Jesse Glick, 2013-09-22, message 'Initial version.'): secrets.child(credentials.getFileName()); secret.copyFrom(...). ZipFileBinding copied the same join later that day in 580c3881e52aaa8aaf5d16f1b35166b1e1028a61. cee2c7b244705c7801eb0091665c9d75a80bdef9 only wrapped a UUID directory around the same join. credentials-binding-plugin root 3bf314aef23085af35b6f1dd091e79df0bfc7534 ('Factored out from plain-credentials.') is a move of those files, not a first-write; 83ba9e2fbf118923af4c8e69115011b1e48cb7bb later extracted AbstractOnDiskBinding.write still calling dir.child(credentials.getFileName()). SECURITY-3672 (3f6decef43ea5eebde2251ec5ea81b7eeeaa21ed, tag 720.v3f6decef43ea_) was the first basename sanitization via new File(...).getName().
